notes.fr: Le mandarin a **quatre tons** : mā (haut et plat), má (montant), mǎ (bas), mà (descendant), plus un ton neutre, court et léger, sans accent : ma. Le ton fait partie du mot : 马 mǎ « cheval », 吗 ma (particule). Écoutez-vous le dire, et exagérez au début.
notes.en: Mandarin has **four tones**: mā (high and level), má (rising), mǎ (low), mà (falling), plus a short, light neutral tone with no mark: ma. The tone is part of the word: 马 mǎ "horse", 吗 ma (a particle). Exaggerate them at first.

notes.fr: 你好 s'écrit nǐ hǎo mais se dit **ní hǎo** : quand deux troisièmes tons se suivent, le premier devient montant. Le pinyin garde le ton du dictionnaire ; c'est à vous de faire le changement (même chose pour 很好 hěn hǎo, dit hén hǎo).
notes.en: 你好 is written nǐ hǎo but said **ní hǎo**: when two third tones meet, the first one rises. Pinyin keeps the dictionary tone and leaves the change to you (likewise 很好 hěn hǎo, said hén hǎo).

notes.fr: **吗** ma à la fin d'une phrase en fait une question fermée (oui / non), sans rien changer d'autre : 你是马克。« Tu es Marc. » → 你是马克吗？« Tu es Marc ? »
notes.en: **吗** ma at the end of a sentence turns it into a yes / no question, with nothing else changed: 你是马克。"You are Marc." → 你是马克吗？"Are you Marc?"

notes.fr: **是** shì « être » relie deux noms. Le verbe ne se conjugue jamais : 我是, 你是 (je suis, tu es). Pour répondre « oui », on reprend le verbe de la question : 是 « (je) suis ».
notes.en: **是** shì "to be" links two nouns. Verbs never change: 我是, 你是 (I am, you are). To answer "yes", repeat the verb of the question: 是 "(I) am".

lessons.title: 守株待兔
lessons.title_en: Waiting by the Stump for a Hare

source.author: 韓非 (c. 280–233 BC)
source.text_from: 《韓非子·五蠹》, as printed in the Hong Kong EDB recommended classical passages (KS1-01); checked against the 古汉语常用字字典 citations

lessons.intro: Han Fei was the great theorist of Legalism, the school that held a state should be run by clear laws and not by appeals to the ancient sage-kings. In the essay "The Five Vermin" (五蠹) he tells this little story to mock rulers who cling to the old ways. It is the most famous fable in Chinese: almost every Chinese schoolchild learns it, and its title became an idiom. Six of the most important words in Classical Chinese appear in its 57 characters: 者, 而, 其, 為, 之, 也.

lines.en: Among the people of Song there was a man who ploughed his fields.
In his field there was a tree stump.
A hare, running, struck the stump,
broke its neck and died.

lines.py: Yīn shì qí lěi ér shǒu zhū,
lines.en: So he put down his plough and kept watch by the stump,
hoping to get another hare.
Hares could not be got again,

lines.py: ér shēn wéi Sòng guó xiào.
lines.en: and he himself became the laughing-stock of Song.
lines.lit: and himself was-by Song state laughed-at

lines.py: Jīn yù yǐ xiān wáng zhī zhèng,
lines.en: Now, to want to use the government of the former kings
to rule the people of the present age —

lines.py: jiē shǒu zhū zhī lèi yě.
lines.en: that is all of the stump-watching kind.

notes.text: **宋** Sòng, a small state in present-day Henan, ruled by descendants of the fallen Shang dynasty. In Warring States anecdotes "a man of Song" is the stock fool: the farmer who pulls up his sprouts to help them grow (揠苗助長, in 孟子) is also from Song.

**有 … 者**, "there was one who …". 者 turns the verb 耕 *to plough* into a noun, "one who ploughs" (compare English *-er*: plough → plough**er**). 有 + V + 者 is the standard way to bring a character on stage: 宋人有耕者 = "among the people of Song, there was a plougher". The place or group (宋人) comes first, as the topic.

**走 = to run**, not "to walk". This is the classic trap of 古今詞義 (old vs. modern meaning): Classical Chinese *walks* with 行 and 步, *runs* with 走, and *hurries* with 趨. Modern 走 has slowed down by one gear. The 說文 already defines 走 as 趨也 "to hurry".

**而** links two verbs or verb phrases: 折頸**而**死 "broke its neck *and (so)* died". It never links two nouns (that's 與). The second 而 in line 5 works the same way: 釋其耒 **而**守株 "put down his plough *and* watched the stump". In line 8, 而 marks a contrast: see n. 9.
**因** here is an adverb, "thereupon, and so", linking the event to what came before. Its core meaning is "to rely on, to follow from", which you will meet as a verb and preposition.

**其** = *his / her / its / their*. In Classical Chinese 其 is mainly a third-person possessive (其耒 "his plough"), not the modern "that, other" of 其他. 耒 lěi is a wooden digging fork, the ancestor of the plough (說文: 手耕曲木也 "a curved wood for tilling by hand").

**冀** jì = "to hope" (modern 希望). **復** fù = "again" (adverb before a verb). *Simplified-character warning:* 复 stands for three different classical words: 復 "return, again", 複 "double, lined (garment)" and 覆 "overturn". Classical texts keep them apart, so the traditional form tells you which word you're reading.

**可 + verb** has a passive sense: 不可復得 "could not be got again". When 可 stands before a transitive verb, the subject is what *receives* the action (兔 the hare is what is "got"). Compare 朽木不可雕也 "rotten wood cannot be carved" (exercise 3).

Three things in one line: **而** here means "and yet / and as a result", with a turn in the story. **身** = "himself, his own person" (not "body"): the hares didn't come back, but *he* became the joke. **為 A V** is a passive: 為宋國笑 "was laughed at by the state of Song" (為 wéi + agent + verb). Later prose often adds 所: 為天下所笑. The 所-less form here is the older one.

**以 X V Y** = "to use X to V Y": 以先王之政，治當世之民 "to use the government of the former kings to rule the people of today". **之** between two nouns marks the first as modifying the second, like modern 的: 先王**之**政 "the former kings' government", 當世**之**民 "the present age's people".

**A，B 也** is the basic Classical judgment sentence, "A is B", with no verb "to be". The whole of lines 9–10 is A; 皆守株之類 "all of the stump-watching kind" is B; 也 closes the judgment. 是 as a copula ("is") is a later development; in Han Fei's time 是 means "this".

The idiom is 守株待兔 "watch the stump, wait for the hare", but 待 *to wait* is not in the original: the four-character form was shaped later. Today it describes anyone who waits for luck instead of working, which is not quite Han Fei's point: he was attacking rulers who apply old policies to a changed world.

lessons.culture: Han Fei (韓非) was a prince of the state of Han and a student of the Confucian Xunzi, yet he became the sharpest critic of Confucian nostalgia. The First Emperor of Qin admired his writings; Han Fei died in a Qin prison in 233 BC, but Qin built its empire on Legalist ideas. "The Five Vermin" names the five kinds of people Han Fei thought were eating the state away: scholars, wandering orators, private swordsmen, courtiers who sell influence, and merchants and artisans.

lessons.title: 自相矛盾

source.author: 韓非 (c. 280–233 BC)
source.text_from: 《韓非子·難一》, as in Japanese Wikibooks 中学校国語 漢文/矛盾 (CC BY-SA), punctuation modernised; closing sentence matched verbatim against several editions. Many Chinese school editions write 盾 for 楯 and read 物莫能陷也 in line 3 (see n. 1, n. 4).

lessons.intro: Han Fei again. In the chapter "Objections I" (難一) he argues that the Confucians can't praise the sage-king Yao as a perfect ruler *and* praise Shun for fixing the problems of Yao's reign: one of the two claims must be false. To make the point he tells this story, which gave Chinese its word for "contradiction", 矛盾 "spear-shield". This lesson's big new idea is the little word 之 placed between a subject and its predicate.

lines.py: Chǔ rén yǒu yù dùn yǔ máo zhě,
lines.en: There was a man of Chu who sold shields and spears.
He praised them, saying:

lines.py: Wú dùn zhī jiān, mò néng xiàn yě.
lines.en: "My shields are so hard that nothing can pierce them."
lines.lit: my shield 's hardness, nothing can pierce

lines.en: Then he praised his spears, saying:

lines.py: Wú máo zhī lì, yú wù wú bù xiàn yě.
lines.en: "My spears are so sharp that there is nothing they can't pierce."
lines.lit: my spear 's sharpness, among things there-is-none not pierced

lines.en: Someone said:

lines.py: Yǐ zǐ zhī máo, xiàn zǐ zhī dùn, hé rú?
lines.en: "What if you used your spear to pierce your shield?"

lines.py: Qí rén fú néng yìng yě.
lines.en: The man could not answer.

lines.h: 夫不可陷之楯與無不陷之矛，
lines.py: Fú bù kě xiàn zhī dùn yǔ wú bù xiàn zhī máo,
lines.en: Now, a shield that cannot be pierced and a spear that pierces everything
lines.h_s: 夫不可陷之楯与无不陷之矛，

lines.py: bù kě tóng shì ér lì.
lines.en: cannot stand together in the same world.

notes.text: **鬻** yù = "to sell" (the everyday word is 賣). **楯** dùn = "shield", written with the wood radical because shields were wooden; later editions and the idiom write **盾**. Both are the same word. 與 joins two nouns: 楯**與**矛 "shields *and* spears" (compare 而, which joins verbs: → L1 n.4).

**之 as an object pronoun**: 譽**之** "praised *them*". After a verb, 之 means him / her / it / them; it can never be a subject. Expect it constantly: 揠之 "pull at them", 求之 "look for it", 飲之 "drink it" in the next lessons. **曰** yuē "to say" introduces direct speech.

**Subject + 之 + predicate.** 吾楯堅 would be a sentence: "my shield is hard". Put 之 between subject and predicate — 吾楯**之**堅 — and the sentence becomes a noun phrase, "the hardness of my shield", which can then be commented on: "(as for) the hardness of my shield — nothing can pierce it". This is one of the most frequent patterns in Classical Chinese; you'll meet it in almost every lesson from now on (吾矛之利 in line 5).

**莫** mò = "nothing / no one": 莫能陷 "nothing can pierce (it)". 莫 is a pronoun that contains its own negation, so there is no 不. 陷 xiàn = "to pierce, break into" (its core meaning is "to fall into a pit"). Many editions read 物莫能陷也, "of things, none can pierce it", with no change in meaning.

**無不 = "there is none that does not" = everything.** 無 "there is no …", 不 "not": two negatives make a strong positive. **於** yú "among, with regard to": 於物 "among things". Compare 莫 in n. 4: the merchant's two boasts are built as mirror images.
**或** huò as a subject = "someone". (In modern Chinese 或 means "or"; that sense exists too, but at the head of a clause 或曰 is "someone said".)

**子** zǐ = "you", a polite address between equals ("sir"). 子之矛 "your spear": here 之 is the ordinary attributive 之 (→ L1 n.10). 以 X V Y "use X to V Y" (→ L1 n.10). **何如** hé rú "how would it be?": the question word 何 comes *before* the verb 如.

**弗** fú is a negative like 不, but typically used before a transitive verb whose object is left out ("could not answer *it*"). 其人 "that man" — 其 as a demonstrative here, not "his" (→ L1 n.6). 應 yìng "to respond".

**夫** fú at the start of a sentence announces a general statement or comment: "Now, …". Read fú, not fū ("man, husband"). Then 不可陷之楯 "a shield that cannot be pierced": a whole verb phrase + 之 + noun = a relative clause (→ L1 n.8 for 不可 + verb).

**同世而立** "stand in the same age". 而 links the manner (同世 "sharing an age") to the verb 立 "to stand" (→ L1 n.4). The idiom 自相矛盾 "to contradict oneself" (lit. "self mutually spear-shield") is a later coinage; the story itself never uses 自相.

glossary.en: not (before a verb, object left out)

lessons.culture: The story is a weapon in a debate. Han Fei's opponents praised both Yao and Shun as perfect sage-kings; Han Fei answers that if Shun had to correct Yao's mistakes, Yao wasn't perfect, and if Yao was perfect, Shun had nothing to correct: "you cannot praise both". The word 矛盾 entered modern Chinese (and Japanese, *mujun*) as the standard term for "contradiction", including the Marxist "contradiction" of Mao's essay 《矛盾論》.

lessons.title: 揠苗助長
lessons.title_en: Pulling Up the Sprouts to Help Them Grow

source.author: 孟子 Mencius (c. 372–289 BC)
source.text_from: 《孟子·公孫丑上》, as quoted on Wiktionary 揠苗助長 (CC BY-SA); lines 1–7 also match the Hong Kong EDB edition.

lessons.intro: Mencius, the second great Confucian, is explaining to a disciple how to nourish one's "flood-like qi" (浩然之氣), the moral courage that grows from always doing what is right. You can't force it, he says, and you mustn't neglect it either, and he tells this story of yet another man of Song. New in this lesson: the particle 矣, which marks something that *has happened* or *has become* the case, and the reading 長 zhǎng "to grow".

lines.h: 宋人有閔其苗之不長而揠之者，
lines.py: Sòng rén yǒu mǐn qí miáo zhī bù zhǎng ér yà zhī zhě,
lines.en: There was a man of Song who, worried that his sprouts weren't growing, tugged at them.
lines.lit: Song people there-was worried his sprouts' not growing and pulled them one
lines.h_s: 宋人有闵其苗之不长而揠之者，

lines.en: He came home, worn out,
and said to his family:
"I'm exhausted today:
I've been helping the sprouts grow!"

lines.py: Qí zǐ qū ér wǎng shì zhī,
lines.en: His son hurried off to look at them;
the sprouts had withered.

lines.h: 天下之不助苗長者寡矣。
lines.py: Tiān xià zhī bù zhù miáo zhǎng zhě guǎ yǐ.
lines.en: In this world, few are those who don't help their sprouts grow.
lines.h_s: 天下之不助苗长者寡矣。

lines.py: Yǐ wéi wú yì ér shě zhī zhě,
lines.en: Those who think it's no use and leave them alone
are those who don't weed their sprouts;
those who help them grow
are those who tug at their sprouts.
Not only is that no use —
it actually harms them.

notes.text: A long first line, built like L1's 宋人有耕者: 宋人 **有** [ … ] **者** "among the people of Song there was one who …" (→ L1 n.2). Inside the brackets: 閔 mǐn "to worry about" (later written 憫) + its object 其苗之不長 "his sprouts' not growing", the subject + 之 + predicate pattern of → L2 n.3. Then 而揠之 "and pulled at them" (→ L1 n.4, L2 n.2).

**長** has two readings. zhǎng = "to grow; to be the elder, to lead"; cháng = "long". Here, and in the idiom 揠苗助長, it is zhǎng. Chinese often marks a change of word by a change of tone or initial (破音字); the dictionary entry for 長 lists them separately.

**-然** rán turns a word into a description of manner: 芒芒然 "in a weary way, worn out". 芒芒 is a reduplicated descriptive word; commentators gloss it as 疲倦的樣子 "looking tired". You'll meet many ~然 words: 忽然, 果然 and 自然 all come from this pattern.
**謂 A 曰** "said to A": 謂 takes the person spoken to as its object. **其人** here is "his household, his family". Compare L2 n.8, where 其人 meant "that man": context decides.

**病** = "exhausted, worn out", not "ill" (古今詞義 → L1 n.3). In early texts 疾 is the ordinary word for illness and 病 a *serious* illness or extreme fatigue. **矣** yǐ marks a new situation: "I'm (now) exhausted". 也 states what *is* (→ L1 n.11); 矣 states what *has come to be*. The story turns on three 矣 (lines 4, 5 and 7): he is tired now, the sprouts have been "helped", and by then they have withered.
**予** yú = "I, me". Classical Chinese has several first-person pronouns: 吾 (L2), 我, 予/余. Here the farmer is boasting.
**趨** qū "to hurry, walk fast" — the middle gear between 行 "walk" and 走 "run" (→ L1 n.3). **往** "to go (to)", **視** "to look at". 而 again links the manner to the action.
**則** zé "then, and so": here it marks what the son *found*: "the sprouts — (by then) they had withered". 槁 gǎo "dried up, withered".

notes.at: 天下之不助苗長者寡矣
notes.text: Mencius turns to the moral. The subject is a long 者-phrase: 天下之 [不助苗長] 者 "those in the world who don't help their sprouts grow", and the predicate is 寡矣 "are few". **寡** guǎ "few" (its opposite is 眾). In other words: almost everyone forces things.
notes.at_s: 天下之不助苗长者寡矣

notes.text: **以為** yǐ wéi "to think, consider that". Here it introduces a whole clause: 以為無益 "think it is no use". (In L6 you will see 以 A 為 B "regard A as B" split around its object.) **捨** shě "to give up, leave alone" (also written 舍).

**A 者，B 者也** — the classic definition sentence: "A is B". Both halves are 者 phrases ("those who …"), and 也 closes the judgment (→ L1 n.11). Lines 9–12 give two of them in parallel: neglecting = not weeding; forcing = tugging.
**非徒 … 而又 …** "not only … but also …". 非 fēi negates a whole statement or a noun ("it is not that …"), whereas 不 negates a verb. 徒 tú "merely, only". 害 "to harm".

glossary.en: final particle: new situation, completed change
to give up, leave alone (= 舍)

lessons.culture: This passage is the second half of Mencius's famous answer on 浩然之氣 (Mencius 2A:2). His advice: keep working at righteousness, "don't forget it, but don't help it grow" (勿忘，勿助長也). The idiom 揠苗助長 (also 拔苗助長 in modern mainland usage) means to spoil something by being too eager, often said of pushy parents and over-ambitious reforms.

lessons.title: 刻舟求劍
lessons.title_en: Notching the Boat to Find the Sword

source.author: compiled under 呂不韋 Lü Buwei (d. 235 BC)
source.text_from: 《呂氏春秋·慎大覽·察今》; first sentence as quoted in 王力《古代漢語》 (with 於 for its 于), the rest matched against two published editions.

lessons.intro: The *Springs and Autumns of Master Lü* is an encyclopedia commissioned by Lü Buwei, chancellor of Qin, from the scholars he kept at his court. The chapter "Examining the Present" (察今) argues the same point as L1: laws must change with the times. This fable brings two important new tools: 所, which turns a verb into "the place / thing that …", and the rhetorical question 不亦…乎.

lines.py: Chǔ rén yǒu shè jiāng zhě,
lines.en: A man of Chu was crossing the river.
lines.lit: Chu people there-was crossing river one

lines.py: qí jiàn zì zhōu zhōng zhuì yú shuǐ,
lines.en: His sword fell from the boat into the water.
At once he cut a notch in the boat, saying:

lines.py: Shì wú jiàn zhī suǒ cóng zhuì.
lines.en: "This is where my sword fell from."
When the boat stopped,

lines.py: cóng qí suǒ qì zhě rù shuǐ qiú zhī.
lines.en: he went into the water from the place he had notched, to look for it.
The boat had moved on,
but the sword had not.
To look for a sword like this —
isn't that foolish?

lines.py: Yǐ cǐ gù fǎ wéi qí guó,
lines.en: To run one's state with these old laws
is just the same.
The times have moved on,
but the laws have not;
to govern like this —
how could it not be hard!

notes.text: **涉** shè "to cross (a river), wade". **江** jiāng is *the* River, the Yangzi, just as 河 is the Yellow River. Only later did 江 and 河 become general words for "river" (古今詞義). 楚人有涉江者 has the same shape as L1's opening (→ L1 n.2).

Two prepositions: **自** "from" (自舟中 "from inside the boat") and **於** "into, at" (墜於水 "fell into the water"). Notice the order: 自 phrases come *before* the verb, 於 phrases *after* it. 墜 zhuì "to fall, drop".
**遽** jù "at once, hastily" (modern 立刻 or 急忙); it shows the man's panic. **契** qì "to carve, notch" (the same word is written 鍥). The modern meaning "contract" comes from notched wooden tallies.
**是 = "this"**, not "is" (→ L1 n.11). 是吾劍之所從墜 is a judgment sentence with no verb: "this [is] the place my sword fell from".

**所 + (preposition) + verb = "the place / thing that …"**. 所 makes a verb into a noun phrase that refers to its object or circumstance: 所墜 "what fell"; 所從墜 "where (something) fell *from*". Put a subject + 之 in front: 吾劍之所從墜 "the place my sword fell from". In line 6, 其所契者 "the place he had notched" adds 者 at the end, with no change of meaning.

**已 … 矣** "already … (now)": 已 yǐ "already" before the verb, 矣 (→ L3 n.5) at the end for the completed change. Two different characters both read yǐ. And **行** here is "to move, go", not "to walk" — it's used of the boat (→ L1 n.3).
**若此** "like this" (若 = 如 "to be like"; 此 "this"). 此 is the ordinary demonstrative "this"; 是 (n. 4) is "this" used to sum up or point back.

**不亦 … 乎** is a rhetorical question expecting "yes": "isn't it (also) …?". You already met it in the first line of the 論語 (→ L1 exercise 2: 不亦說乎). **乎** hū is the question particle; **惑** huò "confused, deluded, foolish".

**故** gù here = "old, former" (故法 "old laws"; compare 故鄉 "old home"). **為** wéi "to manage, run": 為國 "to run a state". 以 A 為 B would be "regard A as B", but here 以此故法 is simply "with these old laws" (→ L1 n.10).
**徙** xǐ "to move, shift" — used of people, capitals, and here of the times. The author mirrors the story: the boat moved, the sword didn't; the times moved, the laws didn't.
**豈 … 哉** "how could …?!": 豈 qǐ starts a rhetorical question, 哉 zāi ends an exclamation. 豈不難哉 "how could it not be difficult!" = it is certainly difficult.

exercise.py: Xué ér shí xí zhī, bù yì yuè hū? Yǒu péng zì yuǎn fāng lái, bù yì lè hū?
exercise.en: To learn and practise it at the right times — is that not a pleasure? To have friends come from afar — is that not a joy?
exercise.tests: 不亦…乎, 自
exercise.h_s: 学而时习之，不亦说乎？有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎？

exercise.en: What you yourself do not want, do not do to others.
exercise.tests: 所 (所不欲 "what one doesn't want"), 於

exercise.en: If this can be tolerated, what cannot?

exercise.en: What passes away is like this, day and night without ceasing!
exercise.tests: 如 = 若, 者, 夫 (exclamatory, at the end)

lessons.culture: Lü Buwei, a merchant, became chancellor of Qin and patron of the young king who would become the First Emperor. He had the book displayed at the gate of the Qin capital and offered a thousand pieces of gold to anyone who could add or remove a single character (一字千金). Like Han Fei, the authors of 察今 argue against copying the laws of the ancient kings: "times change, so laws must change".

lessons.title: 畫蛇添足

source.author: anonymous; compiled by 劉向 Liu Xiang (77–6 BC)
source.text_from: 《戰國策·齊策二·昭陽為楚伐魏》, the standard text, matched against a published edition and the 古汉语常用字字典's quotation of the last line; punctuation modernised.

lessons.intro: The *Intrigues of the Warring States* collects the speeches of travelling persuaders, men who went from court to court selling strategies. Here the persuader 陳軫 Chen Zhen meets a Chu general who has just won a great victory and wants to attack the state of Qi as well. He tells him this story to say: you already have the wine — stop while you're ahead. New in this lesson: the "not yet" negative 未, the question word 安 "how", and 為 meaning "to make".

lines.en: In Chu there was a man who made a sacrifice to his ancestors.

lines.py: cì qí shè rén zhī jiǔ.
lines.en: He gave his retainers a flagon of wine.
The retainers said to one another:

lines.py: Shù rén yǐn zhī bù zú,
lines.en: "For several of us to drink it, it's not enough;

lines.py: yī rén yǐn zhī yǒu yú.
lines.en: for one to drink it, there's more than enough.
Let's each draw a snake on the ground,
and whoever finishes first drinks the wine."
One man's snake was done first.
He pulled the wine towards him and was about to drink it,
but then, holding the flagon in his left hand,
and drawing on the snake with his right, he said:
"I can give it feet!"
Before he had finished,
another man's snake was done.
He snatched the flagon and said:
"Snakes have no feet, of course:

lines.py: zǐ ān néng wéi zhī zú?
lines.en: how can you give it feet?"
And so he drank the wine.
The one who drew feet on the snake
lost his wine in the end.

notes.text: **祠** cí "to make an offering (to ancestors or spirits)". After the rite the sacrificial wine was shared out. 楚有祠者 "in Chu there was one who sacrificed": the 有…者 opening again (→ L1 n.2), this time with a place (楚) as the topic.

**舍人** shè rén "retainers, household men" (舍 "lodging": those who lodged in his house). **卮** zhī is a wine flagon; 卮酒 "a flagon of wine" — the container works as a measure word. **賜** cì "to give (from a superior)". 賜 + person + thing: two objects, as in English "gave his men wine".
**相** xiāng before a verb = "each other, mutually": 相謂 "said to each other". (It can also mean "to someone", as in modern 相信, but here it's reciprocal.)

**數** shù "several" (read shǔ as the verb "to count"). The two lines are a perfect parallel pair: 數人飲之 | 不足 / 一人飲之 | 有餘. **足** "enough" and **餘** "surplus". The whole story will pun on 足, which also means "foot".
**請** qǐng "please (let us) …": a polite proposal. **畫地為蛇** "draw on the ground to make a snake": 為 wéi "to make, to be (as)".
**且** qiě before a verb = "about to": 且飲之 "was about to drink it". (Elsewhere 且 means "and, moreover".) **引** yǐn "to draw, pull towards oneself".
**乃** nǎi "then, thereupon", often with a sense of surprise or contrast: "but then he …". Compare 因 (→ L1 n.5) and 遂 (n. 11).

**為之足** wéi zhī zú "make feet for it": 為 takes two objects, 之 "it (the snake)" and 足 "feet". Some editions and teachers read it wèi zhī zú "draw feet *for* it", with 為 as a preposition; the meaning is the same.
**未** wèi = "not yet". 未成 "(he had) not yet finished". Compare 不 (simple "not") and 弗 (→ L2 n.8). 未 often implies "but it will / should happen".
**固** gù "certainly, by nature, of course": 蛇固無足 "snakes, by their nature, have no feet". **安** ān in line 17 is a question word, "how? where?": 子安能 "how can you …?" — not "peaceful".
**遂** suì "and so, thereupon, then (as a result)". **飲其酒** "drank *his* wine": 其 is the would-be winner's — it was his by rights.

**亡** wáng = "to lose" (and "to flee, to perish"), not only "to die". 終亡其酒 "in the end lost his wine". **終** zhōng "in the end". The idiom 畫蛇添足 "draw a snake and add feet" means to spoil something by overdoing it.

exercise.py: Wèi zhī shēng, yān zhī sǐ?
exercise.en: Not yet understanding life, how could one understand death?
exercise.tests: 未, 焉 = 安 "how"

exercise.py: Wáng yáng ér bǔ láo, wèi wéi chí yě.
exercise.en: To mend the pen after losing a sheep is not yet too late.
exercise.tests: 亡 = lose, 未, 而

exercise.h: 泉涸，魚相與處於陸，相呴以濕，相濡以沫，不如相忘於江湖。
exercise.py: Quán hé, yú xiāng yǔ chǔ yú lù, xiāng xǔ yǐ shī, xiāng rú yǐ mò, bù rú xiāng wàng yú jiāng hú.
exercise.en: When the spring dries up, the fish are left together on dry land; they moisten each other with their breath and wet each other with their spittle. Better to forget each other in the rivers and lakes.
exercise.tests: 相 = each other, 於
exercise.h_s: 泉涸，鱼相与处于陆，相呴以湿，相濡以沫，不如相忘于江湖。

lessons.culture: The frame story: 昭陽 Zhao Yang, chief minister and general of Chu, has crushed Wei and is marching on Qi. Qi sends 陳軫 Chen Zhen to him. After the fable Chen Zhen points out that Zhao Yang already holds the highest rank Chu can give; even if he wins, he gains nothing more, and if he loses, he loses everything — like the man who drew the feet. Zhao Yang turned back.

lessons.title: 狐假虎威
lessons.title_en: The Fox Borrows the Tiger's Might

source.author: anonymous; compiled by 劉向 Liu Xiang (77–6 BC)
source.text_from: 《戰國策·楚策一·江乙對荊宣王》, as printed in 王力《古代漢語》 unit 1; its dash before 猶 is replaced by a comma.

lessons.intro: The first fable told *inside* a conversation, the way persuaders actually used them. King Xuan of Chu (here called 荊, an old name for Chu) asks why the northern states fear his minister Zhao Xixu. Jiang Yi, a rival of Zhao's, answers with a story. Watch three things: the 之 of L2 doing heavy work in long sentences, 以 A 為 B "to regard A as B", and two words, 地方 and 其實, that look modern but aren't.

lines.py: Jīng Xuān wáng wèn qún chén yuē:
lines.en: King Xuan of Jing asked his ministers:

lines.py: Wú wén běi fāng zhī wèi Zhāo Xīxù yě,
lines.en: "I hear that the north fears Zhao Xixu.
Is it really so?"
None of the ministers answered.
Jiang Yi replied:

lines.py: Hǔ qiú bǎi shòu ér shí zhī,
lines.en: "A tiger was hunting all the beasts to eat them,
and caught a fox.

lines.py: Hú yuē: Zǐ wú gǎn shí wǒ yě!
lines.en: The fox said: 'Don't you dare eat me!

lines.py: Tiān dì shǐ wǒ zhǎng bǎi shòu,
lines.en: The Lord of Heaven has made me chief of all the beasts;
if you eat me now,

lines.py: shì nì tiān dì mìng yě.
lines.en: that is defying the Lord of Heaven's command.

lines.py: Zǐ yǐ wǒ wéi bù xìn,
lines.en: If you think I'm lying,
lines.lit: you take me as not truthful

lines.en: I'll walk ahead of you,
you follow behind me,

lines.h: 觀百獸之見我而敢不走乎？』
lines.py: guān bǎi shòu zhī jiàn wǒ ér gǎn bù zǒu hū?
lines.en: and see whether a single beast that sees me dares not run!'
lines.h_s: 观百兽之见我而敢不走乎？』

lines.en: The tiger thought he was right,
so it went along with him.
The beasts saw them and all ran.

lines.py: Hǔ bù zhī shòu wèi jǐ ér zǒu yě,
lines.en: The tiger didn't realise the beasts ran because they feared *it*;
it thought they feared the fox.

lines.py: Jīn wáng zhī dì fāng wǔ qiān lǐ,
lines.en: Now Your Majesty's land is five thousand li on each side,
with a million men in armour,

lines.py: ér zhuān zhǔ zhī Zhāo Xīxù.
lines.en: and you have entrusted them all to Zhao Xixu.

lines.py: Gù běi fāng zhī wèi Xīxù yě,
lines.en: So when the north fears Xixu,

lines.py: qí shí wèi wáng zhī jiǎ bīng yě,
lines.en: what it really fears is Your Majesty's army,

lines.py: yóu bǎi shòu zhī wèi hǔ yě.
lines.en: just as the beasts feared the tiger."

notes.text: **荊** Jīng is another name for Chu (楚). 宣王 King Xuan reigned 369–340 BC. **群臣** "the assembled ministers". The 戰國策 is full of scenes like this: a king asks, the court falls silent, one adviser speaks.

**Subject + 之 + predicate as an object** (→ L2 n.3). 北方畏昭奚恤 would be a sentence, "the north fears Zhao Xixu"; with 之 it becomes a noun phrase, "the north's fearing Zhao Xixu", the object of 聞 "I hear (of)". The final 也 marks a pause before the question. The same pattern returns in lines 15, 24 and 26.
**果** and **誠** both mean "really, truly" (果 survives in 果然 "sure enough"). 何如 "how is it?" (→ L2 n.7).
**莫** "no one" (→ L2 n.4). **對** duì = to reply *to a superior*: ministers 對 the king; the king 問 or 曰.
**食** shí "to eat" (the modern word is 吃). Read sì when it means "to feed someone". 求 here is "to hunt for, look for" (→ L4).
**無** here = **毋** wú "don't!": a prohibition. 子無敢食我也 "don't you dare eat me". Classical Chinese uses 無/毋 and 勿 for "don't", where modern Chinese says 別 or 不要.
**使 A V** "make A do V, have A V": a causative. **長** zhǎng (→ L3 n.2) "chief" used as a verb: 長百獸 "to be chief of the hundred beasts". 百獸 "the hundred beasts" = all animals.
**是** = "this (that you'd be doing)" (→ L4 n.4). 是逆天帝命也 "this is defying the Lord of Heaven's command" — 也 closes the judgment (→ L1 n.11). **逆** nì "to go against, defy".

**以 A 為 B** "to regard A as B": 以我為不信 "regard me as untruthful". Two lines later, 以為 (→ L3 n.10) "to think" is the same structure with the A left out: 虎以為然 "the tiger considered (it) right". **信** xìn "truthful, trustworthy"; **然** rán "so, right".

**為** wèi "for, on behalf of": 為子先行 "walk ahead for you". Contrast 為 wéi "to be, to make" (L4, L5). And **行** = "walk" vs **走** = "run" (line 15): both in the same breath, the clearest proof of → L1 n.3.
**敢不 V 乎** "dare not V?": a rhetorical question meaning "none will dare *not* run" = they will all run. **觀** guān "to observe, watch".
**己** jǐ "oneself": 畏己 "feared *it* (the tiger itself)". 己 refers back to the subject of the main clause, 虎.

**地方 is two words!** Read 地 | 方五千里: "(your) land — five thousand li square", i.e. five thousand li from east to west and from north to south. Modern 地方 "place" is a later compound; reading it here would be a classic 古今 mistake. (A 里 lǐ was roughly 400 m.)
**帶甲** "wearing armour" = armoured soldiers. **屬** zhǔ (line 23) "to entrust": 專屬之昭奚恤 "entrust them solely to Zhao Xixu", with 之 = "them" (the million soldiers) and 昭奚恤 as the second object.

**其實** = "the reality of it", not the modern adverb "actually". The sentence is: [北方之畏 奚恤也] subject, [其實] "its reality", [畏王之甲兵也] predicate: "the north's fearing Xixu — the truth of it is fearing Your Majesty's armies". 甲兵 "armour and weapons" = the army.
**猶** yóu "to be like, just as" (also "still"). Jiang Yi closes by mapping the fable onto the court: king = tiger, Zhao Xixu = fox. That's the persuader's art: never say it directly.

lessons.culture: The fox's trick gave Chinese the idiom 狐假虎威 "the fox borrows the tiger's majesty" (假 jiǎ "to borrow" — the word itself is not in the story). It is used of underlings who throw their weight around on the strength of a powerful patron. Jiang Yi's real target was his rival Zhao Xixu: by reminding the king whose power it really was, he cut Zhao down to size.

lessons.title: 複習一
lessons.intro: Six fables, about 300 characters, and most of the machinery of Classical Chinese prose is already in place. Re-read the six texts once more, aloud, with Cover on. Then go through the points below: each one sends you back to the note where it was first explained. Finish with the exercise: six new sentences from the 論語, using only what you've met.

recap.topic: 有 … 者: bringing a character on stage
recap.text: Place or group + 有 + verb phrase + 者 = "there was one (from X) who …". Every fable but L6 opens this way: 宋人有耕者 · 楚人有鬻楯與矛者 · 宋人有閔其苗之不長而揠之者 · 楚人有涉江者 · 楚有祠者.

(1) between two nouns, like 的: 先王之政. (2) after a verb, "him / it / them": 譽之, 求之. (3) between subject and predicate, turning a sentence into a noun phrase: 吾楯之堅 "the hardness of my shield", 北方之畏昭奚恤 "the north's fearing Zhao Xixu". (4) as a verb, "to go to" — not seen yet, but coming.
也 closes a statement of what *is*: 皆守株之類也, A者 B者也. 矣 marks what *has come to be*: 今日病矣, 苗則槁矣, 舟已行矣. A sentence with no verb + 也 is the Classical "A is B"; 是 still means "this".

不 plain "not" · 弗 "not (it)" · 未 "not yet" · 非 "it is not that" · 無/毋 "there is no; don't!" — plus 莫 "no one / nothing", a pronoun with the negation built in. Double negatives make strong positives: 無不陷 "pierces everything".
者 follows a verb phrase: "one who V's" (耕者, 先成者, 為蛇足者). 所 precedes a verb: "what / where one V's" (所從墜 "where it fell from", 所契 "what he'd notched").

recap.topic: Words that changed meaning (古今詞義)
recap.text: 走 run (not walk) · 行 walk / move · 趨 hurry · 病 exhausted · 江 the Yangzi · 亡 lose · 身 oneself · 地方 "land … square" · 其實 "the reality of it".
不亦…乎 "isn't it …?" · 豈…哉 "how could …!" · 安 "how?" · 敢不…乎 "would dare not …?". All of them expect the listener to agree.
以 X V "use X to V" · 以 A 為 B "regard A as B" · 以為 "think that". 為 wéi "to be, make, run" · 為 wèi "for" · 為 A V "be V'ed by A" (passive).

lessons.title: 落花生

source.author: 許地山 (1894–1941)
source.text_from: 《許地山作品選集》(好讀出版), as excerpted by 遠見 gvm.com.tw/article/60672; compared line by line on 2026-11-12

lessons.intro: Xu Dishan was born in Tainan in 1894; his family left Taiwan for Fujian after the Japanese takeover the next year. He became a scholar of religion, ended his career as professor of Chinese at the University of Hong Kong, and signed his fiction 落華生, "Peanut". This essay was published in 1922 and has been in Chinese school readers ever since. The sentences are short and the story is a family evening, which makes it a good first step: nearly every word you don't know here is a *written* word, the layer of vocabulary that starts where the HSK 5 stopped. Watch the five words built on 然.

lines.en: Behind our house there was half a mu of unused ground.

lines.h: 母親說：「讓它荒蕪著怪可惜，既然你們那麼愛吃花生，就闢來做花生園罷。」
lines.en: Mother said, "It's rather a shame to leave it lying waste. Since you're all so fond of peanuts, let's clear it and make a peanut garden."
lines.h_s: 母亲说：「让它荒芜著怪可惜，既然你们那么爱吃花生，就辟来做花生园罢。」

lines.h: 我們幾姊弟和幾個小丫頭都很喜歡——買種的買種，動土的動土，灌園的灌園；
lines.en: We children and the few young maids were all delighted. Some bought seed, some dug the ground, some watered the plot;
lines.h_s: 我们几姊弟和几个小丫头都很喜欢——买种的买种，动土的动土，灌园的灌园；

lines.h: 過不了幾個月，居然收穫了！
lines.en: and before many months had gone by, to our surprise, there was a harvest!
lines.h_s: 过不了几个月，居然收获了！

lines.h: 媽媽說：「今晚我們可以做一個收穫節，也請你們爹爹來嘗嘗我們的新花生，如何？」
lines.en: Mama said, "Tonight we could hold a harvest festival, and ask your father to come and taste our new peanuts. What do you say?"
lines.h_s: 妈妈说：「今晚我们可以做一个收获节，也请你们爹爹来尝尝我们的新花生，如何？」

lines.en: We all agreed.

lines.h: 母親把花生做成好幾樣的食品，還吩咐這節期要在園裡的茅亭舉行。
lines.en: Mother made the peanuts into a good many dishes, and gave word that the festival was to be held in the thatched pavilion in the garden.
lines.h_s: 母亲把花生做成好几样的食品，还吩咐这节期要在园里的茅亭举行。

lines.h: 那晚上的天色不大好，可是爹爹也到來，實在很難得！
lines.en: The sky was not very promising that evening, but Father came all the same, which was a rare thing indeed!
lines.h_s: 那晚上的天色不大好，可是爹爹也到来，实在很难得！

lines.h: 爹爹說：「你們愛吃花生麼？」
lines.en: Father said, "Do you like eating peanuts?"
lines.h_s: 爹爹说：「你们爱吃花生么？」

lines.en: We all raced to answer, "We do!"
"Who can tell me what is good about the peanut?"

lines.h: 姊姊說：「花生的氣味很美。」
lines.en: Elder sister said, "Peanuts have a lovely flavour."
lines.h_s: 姊姊说：「花生的气味很美。」

lines.en: Elder brother said, "You can make oil from peanuts."

lines.h: 我說：「無論何等人都可以用賤價買它來吃；都喜歡吃它。這就是它的好處。」
lines.en: I said, "People of every sort can buy them cheaply to eat, and everyone likes them. That is what's good about them."
lines.h_s: 我说：「无论何等人都可以用贱价买它来吃；都喜欢吃它。这就是它的好处。」

lines.h: 爹爹說：「花生的用處固然很多，但有一樣是很可貴的。
lines.en: Father said, "The peanut has many uses, to be sure, but one thing about it is truly precious.
lines.h_s: 爹爹说：「花生的用处固然很多，但有一样是很可贵的。

lines.h: 這小小的豆不像那好看的蘋果、桃子、石榴，把它們的果實懸在枝上，
lines.en: This little bean is not like the handsome apple, peach and pomegranate, which hang their fruit on the branch,
lines.h_s: 这小小的豆不像那好看的苹果、桃子、石榴，把它们的果实悬在枝上，

lines.h: 鮮紅嫩綠的顏色，令人一望而發生羨慕的心。
lines.en: bright red and tender green, so that one look is enough to make people admire them.
lines.lit: causing people, at one glance, to have an admiring heart arise
lines.h_s: 鲜红嫩绿的颜色，令人一望而发生羡慕的心。

lines.h: 它只把果子埋在地下，等到成熟，才容人把它挖出來。
lines.en: It just buries its fruit in the ground, and only when it is ripe does it let anyone dig it up.
lines.h_s: 它只把果子埋在地下，等到成熟，才容人把它挖出来。

lines.h: 你們偶然看見一棵花生瑟縮地長在地上，不能立刻辨出它有沒有果實，
lines.en: If you happen to see a peanut plant huddled low on the ground, you can't tell straight away whether it has any fruit;
lines.h_s: 你们偶然看见一棵花生瑟缩地长在地上，不能立刻辨出它有没有果实，

lines.h: 必得等到你接觸它才能知道。」
lines.en: you have to wait until you touch it to know."
lines.h_s: 必得等到你接触它才能知道。」

lines.h: 我們都說：「是的。」母親也點點頭。
lines.en: We all said, "That's true." Mother nodded too.
lines.h_s: 我们都说：「是的。」母亲也点点头。

lines.h: 爹爹接下去說：「所以你們要像花生，因為它是有用的，不是偉大、好看的東西。」
lines.en: Father went on, "So you must be like the peanut, because it is a useful thing, not a grand or good-looking one."
lines.h_s: 爹爹接下去说：「所以你们要像花生，因为它是有用的，不是伟大、好看的东西。」

lines.h: 我說：「那麼，人要做有用的人，不要做偉大、體面的人了。」
lines.en: I said, "Then a person should be a useful person, and not a great or grand-looking one."
lines.h_s: 我说：「那么，人要做有用的人，不要做伟大、体面的人了。」

lines.h: 爹爹說：「這是我對於你們的希望。」
lines.en: Father said, "That is what I hope for you."
lines.h_s: 爹爹说：「这是我对于你们的希望。」

lines.en: We talked until the night was nearly over before we parted.

lines.h: 所有花生食品雖然沒有了，然而父親的話現在還印在我心版上。
lines.en: All the peanut dishes are long gone, yet Father's words are printed on my heart to this day.
lines.h_s: 所有花生食品虽然没有了，然而父亲的话现在还印在我心版上。

notes.text: **隙** xì is a crack or gap (空隙, 縫隙), so 隙地 is the bit of land left over between things: a spare plot. In speech you would say 空地. This is the pattern of the whole lesson: a one-character classical word (隙) living on inside a two-character written one.

**怪** as an adverb, "rather, quite", is colloquial northern usage, normally 怪…的 (怪可惜的). **可惜** is 可 + verb, "worth regretting": the same 可 as in 可貴 "worth prizing" (line 15), 可愛, 可怕, 可笑. In Classical Chinese this 可 is still a free word with a passive sense (→ 文言 L1 n.8).

**既然 … 就 …** "since (it is already the case that) …, then …". 既 jì is classical for "already, having done". The 然 is the first of five in this text: 既然, 居然, 固然, 雖然, 然而. Classical 然 means "so, like that"; stuck onto a word it makes "in such a way" (→ 文言 L3 n.3), and that is how the written language builds its adverbs and conjunctions.

**闢** pì "to open up, clear (land)", as in 開闢. Careful with the simplified form: 辟 stands for two different words, 闢 pì "open up" and 辟 bì "sovereign; to ward off" (復辟 fùbì "restoration of a monarch").
**罷** here is the particle *ba*, today written 吧. Writers of the 1920s wrote 罷 for it, and 麼 for 嗎 (line 9: 愛吃花生麼？). Both are read as the modern particles. As a full word 罷 is bà "to stop" (罷工, 罷了).

**A 的 A, B 的 B** "some did A, some did B": each 的 phrase is "the ones who …". 種 is zhǒng "seed" here, not zhòng "to plant". 動土 "break ground" and 灌園 "water the garden" are verb + object in the classical way, one character each.
**居然** "unexpectedly, against what one would think". The children are amazed their own work produced anything. Its near-twin 竟然 is a little stronger and can be used for bad surprises.

In the first printing (《小說月報》, 1922) this was 我們**底**新花生, and the last line 父親**底**話. For some years in the 1920s many writers kept 的 for descriptions (好看的蘋果) and wrote 底 for possession. Later editions, like ours, print 的 throughout; in an old edition of 魯迅 or 許地山 you will meet 底 on every page.
**如何** at the end of a proposal: "how about it?". It is the classical question 何如 / 如何, "what is it like?" (→ 文言 L6 n.3), and still the normal written word for 怎麼樣.

**吩咐** fēnfù "to give instructions" (to children, servants, juniors). 節期 "the time of a festival" is rare; the "harvest festival" is the mother's own invention. 茅亭 is a pavilion roofed with 茅 máo, thatch grass.

**何等** "what kind, what rank of": 何 is the classical "what". Today 何等 is mostly an exclamation, "how very" (何等重要!). **賤價** "low price": 賤 keeps its oldest sense, "cheap", the opposite of 貴; in today's speech it is mostly an insult.
**固然 …, 但 …** "admittedly …, but …": the speaker grants a point before making his own. 固 is classical "certainly, by nature" (→ 文言 L5 n.10: 蛇固無足).

notes.at: 令人一望而發生羨慕的心
notes.text: Three written features in one clause. **令** "to cause, make" is the written word for 讓 / 叫 (令人感動). **一 … 而 …** "at a single …, then …": 而 joins two verbs exactly as in Classical Chinese (→ 文言 L1 n.4). And **發生** means "to arise, come into being"; today it is nearly always "to happen". 羨慕的心 is the classical 羨慕之心 with 的 for 之.
notes.at_s: 令人一望而发生羡慕的心

notes.text: **容** "to allow, permit", as in 不容 "does not allow", 容許, 容忍. 才容人 "only then does it let people …".

**瑟縮** sèsuō "huddled, shrinking (as if from cold)". Both syllables begin with s-: it is an alliterative two-syllable word of the classical type, where the sound carries the picture and the characters cannot be translated one by one (compare 彷彿, 徘徊, 參差).
**必得** bìděi "must, have no choice but to". 得 is děi "must", not dé "to get".
**於** yú is the all-purpose classical preposition, "at, in, to, with regard to" (→ 文言 L2 n.5). Written Chinese keeps it inside 對於, 關於, 由於, 至於, 等於, and on its own after a verb: 生於台南 "born in Tainan".
**闌** lán "nearly over, at its end". 夜闌 "deep in the night" is a poetic word; the four-character phrase 夜闌人靜 "the night far gone and everyone quiet" is where you will meet it most.

**雖然 …, 然而 …** "although …, yet …". 然而 is literally "so, and yet": it is the written "but", heavier than 但是 or 可是, and it usually opens the clause that matters most. **心版** is "the printing block of the heart": 版 is a woodblock, which is why the words are 印, printed, on it.

lessons.title: 對稱
lessons.intro: Many everyday 成語 are built on a frame that repeats: 一X一Y, 無X無Y, 所X所Y, 胡X亂Y. Once you see the frame, you only have to learn the two halves, which usually say the same thing twice (全心全意 "whole heart, whole mind") or repeat a word (日復一日 "day comes back to day"). Learn the frames, not just the words: the same frames make hundreds of rarer 成語.

frames.en: X and Y are near-synonyms; 一 = 'one, the same, every'
whole X, whole Y: total commitment
negation twice: 'without X or Y'
所 + verb = 'what one Xs' (classical nominaliser, → lesson 3)

lessons.title: 數字
lessons.intro: Numbers in 成語 are almost never real counts. 一 means "the whole, the same, once, at once", 七八 means "all over the place", 千 and 萬 mean "countless", 四面八方 "every direction". Paired numbers (一清二楚, 亂七八糟) give rhythm more than meaning. The last few items of the lesson are about wholes and pieces (從頭到尾, 支離破碎), the same idea without numbers.

frames.en: 'one…two…': completely, thoroughly
'seven…eight…': in a mess, all over
thousands, tens of thousands: countless
not a single X (→ 所, lesson 3)
alone one, no second: unique

lessons.title: 虛詞
lessons.intro: Modern Chinese keeps a handful of classical function words alive, mostly inside 成語. Learn these five and a large share of 成語 become readable: 所 + verb "what one Vs", 而 "and, and then, yet", 之 "of" (= 的), 以 "by means of, in order to", 於 "at, to, than" (= 在, 對, 比). Two more appear here: 其 "its, his, their" and 諸 "all the, the various". These are the same words the main Wenyan course teaches in its first lessons.

frames.en: 'what one Vs', a noun: 前所未有 'what before has-not-had'
而 links two actions: 'and then' or 'yet'
之 = 的: 'the Y of X'
以 = 'with, by means of, so as to'
於 = 'to, at, for'
其 = 'its, their'; 諸 = 'all the, the various'

lessons.title: 否定
lessons.title_en: Saying no: 不 and 無
lessons.intro: Negation is the most common building block of high-frequency 成語. 不 negates a verb or an adjective ("not"), 無 negates having ("without, there is no"). The negative often comes second or third, with the structure of classical Chinese: 迫不及待 "pressed, not able to wait", 微不足道 "small, not worth mentioning". The lesson ends with three ways of saying "unexpected" (意想不到, 出乎意料, 出人意料), the kind of near-synonym set teachers in China and Taiwan like to drill.

lessons.title: 對稱與數字
lessons.intro: The frames of lessons 1 and 2 come back, with new members. 一 is again "whole, single, at once": 一針見血 "one needle, and blood shows", 一觸即發 "one touch and it goes off". Two new frames: X然一新 "brand new", and A來B去-type pairs of opposites that cover the whole range (大街小巷 "big streets and small lanes" = everywhere).

lessons.title: 虛詞（二）
lessons.intro: More 文言 function words, frozen inside modern 成語. 而 again links two verbs ("and, and then, yet"). 之 is now also an object pronoun "it" (持之以恆 "hold it with constancy"). 以 marks the means or the purpose (以身作則 "with one's own person, make a model"). 其 is "its, the" and 可 + verb is "can be V-ed" (屈指可數 "can be counted on the fingers"). 所 + verb, from lesson 3, turns a verb into "what one Vs".

frames.en: 而 joins a manner or a first action to the main verb

'its, his, the'
'nothing that can be V-ed' / 'can be V-ed'
'what one Vs' / 'the N of'

ex.h_s: 当代小品通过中央电视台春节联欢晚会的近20年的推广，取得了很大的进步，成为观众喜闻乐见的一个艺术形式。

origin.text: 歲亦無恙耶？民亦無恙耶？王亦無恙耶？
origin.text_s: 岁亦无恙耶？民亦无恙耶？王亦无恙耶？

items.note: The Queen Dowager of Zhao asks the envoy of Qi, in this order, whether the harvest, the people and the king are well. Then she explains why the king comes last.

ex.h: 商人看見貝兒能夠安然無恙地回來不斷的擁抱著她不放。
ex.py: Shāng rén kàn jiàn Bèi'ér néng gòu ān rán wú yàng de huí lái bù duàn de yōng bào zhe tā bù fàng.
ex.en: When the merchant saw Belle come back safe and sound, he hugged her and wouldn't let go.
ex.h_t: 商人看見貝兒能夠安然無恙地回來不斷的擁抱著她不放。
ex.h_s: 商人看见贝儿能够安然无恙地回来不断的拥抱著她不放。

ex.h: 入侵的日軍被打得措手不及，將领来岛通总也被击毙。
ex.py: Rù qīn de Rì jūn bèi dǎ de cuò shǒu bù jí, jiàng lǐng Láidǎo Tōngzǒng yě bèi jī bì.
ex.en: The invading Japanese were caught off guard, and their commander Kurushima Michifusa was killed.
ex.h_t: 入侵的日軍被打得措手不及，將領來島通總也被擊斃。
ex.h_s: 入侵的日军被打得措手不及，将领来岛通总也被击毙。

items.note: 刻 was a unit of time (a hundredth of a day).

ex.h: 楊大郎明白母親苦衷，但父親有難刻不容緩，故向母親許下諾言，必會帶領老父和眾弟平安回家。
ex.py: Yáng Dàláng míng bái mǔ qīn kǔ zhōng, dàn fù qīn yǒu nán kè bù róng huǎn, gù xiàng mǔ qīn xǔ xià nuò yán, bì huì dài lǐng lǎo fù hé zhòng dì píng ān huí jiā.
ex.en: Yang the eldest understood his mother's concerns, but his father was in danger and there was no time to lose, so he promised her he would bring his father and brothers home safe.
ex.h_t: 楊大郎明白母親苦衷，但父親有難刻不容緩，故向母親許下諾言，必會帶領老父和眾弟平安回家。
ex.h_s: 杨大郎明白母亲苦衷，但父亲有难刻不容缓，故向母亲许下诺言，必会带领老父和众弟平安回家。

ex.h: 再加上馆舍三次火灾的发生，让新馆的建设迫在眉睫。
ex.py: Zài jiā shàng guǎn shě sān cì huǒ zāi de fā shēng, ràng xīn guǎn de jiàn shè pò zài méi jié.
ex.en: On top of that, the building caught fire three times, which made a new library extremely urgent.
ex.h_t: 再加上館舍三次火災的發生，讓新館的建設迫在眉睫。
ex.h_s: 再加上馆舍三次火灾的发生，让新馆的建设迫在眉睫。

ex.h: 僵尸审判作为中世纪教廷最为骇人听闻的片段之一而载入史册。
ex.py: Jiāng shī shěn pàn zuò wéi zhōng shì jì jiào tíng zuì wéi hài rén tīng wén de piàn duàn zhī yī ér zǎi rù shǐ cè.
ex.en: The Cadaver Synod went down in history as one of the most appalling episodes of the medieval papacy.
ex.h_t: 殭屍審判作為中世紀教廷最為駭人聽聞的片段之一而載入史冊。
ex.h_s: 僵尸审判作为中世纪教廷最为骇人听闻的片段之一而载入史册。

items.note: 諱 "to avoid (a name)": the names of rulers and parents were taboo, 諱.

ex.h: 公众终于对关于空气污染的意见直言不讳了。
ex.py: Gōng zhòng zhōng yú duì guān yú kōng qì wū rǎn de yì jiàn zhí yán bù huì le.
ex.en: The public has finally spoken out frankly about air pollution.
ex.h_t: 公眾終於對關於空氣汙染的意見直言不諱了。
ex.h_s: 公众终于对关于空气污染的意见直言不讳了。

ex.h: 樂觀而有野心，不太在意細節，決定目標便會勇往直前。
ex.py: Lè guān ér yǒu yě xīn, bù tài zài yì xì jié, jué dìng mù biāo biàn huì yǒng wǎng zhí qián.
ex.en: Optimistic and ambitious, not much bothered by details, they forge ahead once they've set a goal.
ex.h_t: 樂觀而有野心，不太在意細節，決定目標便會勇往直前。
ex.h_s: 乐观而有野心，不太在意细节，决定目标便会勇往直前。

lessons.title: 典故
lessons.intro: Every 成語 here has a story or a precise source behind it: a seller of spears and shields (自相矛盾), a poet at the river where Xiang Yu died (捲土重來), two princes splitting the road to Luoyang (分道揚鑣). You can use them without knowing the story, but the story is what makes them stick. 自相矛盾 is taught in full, from the 韓非子 text, in the main course.

items.note: A man of Chu praised his shield (nothing can pierce it) and his spear (it pierces anything). "What if your spear strikes your shield?" He had no answer.

ex.h: 你在自相矛盾。
ex.py: Nǐ zài zì xiāng máo dùn.
ex.en: You're contradicting yourself.
ex.h_t: 你在自相矛盾。
ex.h_s: 你在自相矛盾。

origin.text: 江東子弟多才俊，卷土重來未可知
origin.text_s: 江东子弟多才俊，卷土重来未可知

items.note: Du Mu at the place where Xiang Yu killed himself rather than retreat. The young men east of the river were talented; he might have come back. The source writes 卷 for 捲.

ex.h: 随着一战的结束，列强卷土重来，中国经济迅速转向萧条。
ex.py: Suí zhe Yī Zhàn de jié shù, liè qiáng juǎn tǔ chóng lái, Zhōngguó jīng jì xùn sù zhuǎn xiàng xiāo tiáo.
ex.en: When the First World War ended, the great powers came back, and China's economy quickly fell into depression.
ex.h_t: 隨著一戰的結束，列強捲土重來，中國經濟迅速轉向蕭條。
ex.h_s: 随着一战的结束，列强卷土重来，中国经济迅速转向萧条。

origin.text: 先即制人，後則為人所制
origin.text_s: 先即制人，后则为人所制

ex.h: 田令孜认为杨师立会反对自己和陈敬瑄，决定先发制人。
ex.py: Tián Lìngzī rèn wéi Yáng Shīlì huì fǎn duì zì jǐ hé Chén Jìngxuān, jué dìng xiān fā zhì rén.
ex.en: Tian Lingzi thought Yang Shili would turn against him and Chen Jingxuan, and decided to strike first.
ex.h_t: 田令孜認為楊師立會反對自己和陳敬瑄，決定先發制人。
ex.h_s: 田令孜认为杨师立会反对自己和陈敬瑄，决定先发制人。

origin.text: 洛陽我之豐沛，自應分路揚鑣
origin.text_s: 洛阳我之丰沛，自应分路扬镳

items.note: Two officials quarrelled over which of them should give way in the streets of Luoyang. The emperor ruled that from then on they should take separate roads. 鑣 is the bit of a horse.

ex.h: 罗明远把白求恩交给了护送部队，两人就此分道扬镳了。
ex.py: Luó Míngyuǎn bǎ Báiqiú'ēn jiāo gěi le hù sòng bù duì, liǎng rén jiù cǐ fēn dào yáng biāo le.
ex.en: Luo Mingyuan handed Bethune over to the escort, and there the two parted ways.
ex.h_t: 羅明遠把白求恩交給了護送部隊，兩人就此分道揚鑣了。
ex.h_s: 罗明远把白求恩交给了护送部队，两人就此分道扬镳了。

ex.h: 張惠妹因為張雨生的協助，從默默無名成為家喻戶曉的歌手。
ex.py: Zhāng Huìmèi yīn wèi Zhāng Yǔshēng de xié zhù, cóng mò mò wú míng chéng wéi jiā yù hù xiǎo de gē shǒu.
ex.en: With Tom Chang's help, A-mei went from unknown to a household name.
ex.h_t: 張惠妹因為張雨生的協助，從默默無名成為家喻戶曉的歌手。
ex.h_s: 张惠妹因为张雨生的协助，从默默无名成为家喻户晓的歌手。

items.en: tit for tat, in direct opposition

origin.text: 夫一切問答，如針鋒相投
origin.text_s: 夫一切问答，如针锋相投

items.note: Zen at first. A good question-and-answer meets "like needle point to needle point", in perfect agreement. Now it means the reverse, direct confrontation.

ex.h: 言談之間時常與長歌針鋒相對，但實際上相當疼惜她。
ex.py: Yán tán zhī jiān shí cháng yǔ Chánggē zhēn fēng xiāng duì, dàn shí jì shàng xiàng dāng téng xī tā.
ex.en: When they talk, he is always at odds with Chang'ge, but in fact he cares for her a great deal.
ex.h_t: 言談之間時常與長歌針鋒相對，但實際上相當疼惜她。
ex.h_s: 言谈之间时常与长歌针锋相对，但实际上相当疼惜她。

origin.text: 皆白裳、白旂、素甲、白羽之矰，望之如荼
origin.text_s: 皆白裳、白旗、素甲、白羽之矰，望之如荼

items.note: King Fuchai of Wu's army, one square all in white "like 荼 (reed flowers)", one all in red "like fire". It was a show of strength.

ex.h: 戰爭如火如荼。
ex.py: Zhàn zhēng rú huǒ rú tú.
ex.en: The war is raging.
ex.h_t: 戰爭如火如荼。
ex.h_s: 战争如火如荼。

origin.text: 軒然大波起，宇宙隘而妨
origin.text_s: 轩然大波起，宇宙隘而妨

ex.h: 琅威理返回英国后，宣传他在华受辱的经历，引起轩然大波。
ex.py: Láng Wēilǐ fǎn huí Yīngguó hòu, xuān chuán tā zài Huá shòu rǔ de jīng lì, yǐn qǐ xuān rán dà bō.
ex.en: Back in Britain, Lang publicised the humiliations he had suffered in China, causing an uproar.
ex.h_t: 琅威理返回英國後，宣傳他在華受辱的經歷，引起軒然大波。
ex.h_s: 琅威理返回英国后，宣传他在华受辱的经历，引起轩然大波。

items.en: a walking corpse, a living dead

origin.text: 不學者雖存，謂之行尸走肉耳
origin.text_s: 不学者虽存，谓之行尸走肉耳

items.note: First said of people who don't study. 尸 is the old form of 屍.

ex.h: 他已形同行屍走肉。
ex.py: Tā yǐ xíng tóng xíng shī zǒu ròu.
ex.en: He's become a walking corpse.
ex.h_t: 他已形同行屍走肉。
ex.h_s: 他已形同行尸走肉。

items.en: to make something up out of nothing

origin.text: 天下萬物生於有，有生於無
origin.text_s: 天下万物生于有，有生于无

items.note: In 老子, being comes from non-being. Now it means a fabrication, the opposite of a compliment.

ex.h: 这完全是无中生有的东西。
ex.py: Zhè wán quán shì wú zhōng shēng yǒu de dōng xī.
ex.en: This is a complete fabrication.
ex.h_t: 這完全是無中生有的東西。
ex.h_s: 这完全是无中生有的东西。

ex.h: 這種敵對的稱呼和態度，在《朝鮮王朝實錄》中比比皆是。
ex.py: Zhè zhǒng dí duì de chēng hū hé tài dù, zài «Cháoxiǎn Wángcháo Shílù» zhōng bǐ bǐ jiē shì.
ex.en: Such hostile names and attitudes are everywhere in the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty.
ex.h_t: 這種敵對的稱呼和態度，在《朝鮮王朝實錄》中比比皆是。
ex.h_s: 这种敌对的称呼和态度，在《朝鲜王朝实录》中比比皆是。

items.en: to live in peace and work happily

ex.h: 王延彬治理泉州期間，官员和民众安居乐业，粮食连年丰收。
ex.py: Wáng Yánbīn zhì lǐ Quánzhōu qī jiān, guān yuán hé mín zhòng ān jū lè yè, liáng shí lián nián fēng shōu.
ex.en: While Wang Yanbin governed Quanzhou, officials and people lived in peace, with good harvests year after year.
ex.h_t: 王延彬治理泉州期間，官員和民眾安居樂業，糧食連年豐收。
ex.h_s: 王延彬治理泉州期间，官员和民众安居乐业，粮食连年丰收。

origin.text: 建久安之勢，成長治之業
origin.text_s: 建久安之势，成长治之业

ex.h: 在上者要施行的政务能办到，在下者能胜任交办的公务，因此国家才能长治久安。
ex.py: Zài shàng zhě yào shī xíng de zhèng wù néng bàn dào, zài xià zhě néng shèng rèn jiāo bàn de gōng wù, yīn cǐ guó jiā cái néng cháng zhì jiǔ ān.
ex.en: Only when those above can carry out their policies, and those below can do the work given them, does a state enjoy lasting peace.
ex.h_t: 在上者要施行的政務能辦到，在下者能勝任交辦的公務，因此國家才能長治久安。
ex.h_s: 在上者要施行的政务能办到，在下者能胜任交办的公务，因此国家才能长治久安。

items.en: to cry out, to call loudly for
items.note: Han Yu, petitioning the chief minister for a post, compares himself to a drowning man shouting for help.

ex.h: 姜昆称，“如果在路上，看到有人在往相反的方向走，我们必须大声疾呼，把他们叫回来。
ex.py: Jiāng Kūn chēng, “rú guǒ zài lù shàng, kàn dào yǒu rén zài wǎng xiāng fǎn de fāng xiàng zǒu, wǒ men bì xū dà shēng jí hū, bǎ tā men jiào huí lái.
ex.src: wikipedia: 郭德纲徒弟打人事件
ex.en: Jiang Kun said, 'If we see someone on the road walking the wrong way, we have to call out loudly and bring them back.'
ex.h_t: 姜昆稱，“如果在路上，看到有人在往相反的方向走，我們必須大聲疾呼，把他們叫回來。
ex.h_s: 姜昆称，“如果在路上，看到有人在往相反的方向走，我们必须大声疾呼，把他们叫回来。

items.en: to make a bad situation worse

ex.h: 达濠为日占领，更是雪上加霜，地方饥馑严重，饿殍遍野。
ex.py: Dáháo wéi Rì zhàn lǐng, gèng shì xuě shàng jiā shuāng, dì fāng jī jǐn yán zhòng, è piǎo biàn yě.
ex.en: Dahao's occupation by Japan made things even worse: famine was severe and the starving lay everywhere.
ex.h_t: 達濠為日佔領，更是雪上加霜，地方饑饉嚴重，餓殍遍野。
ex.h_s: 达濠为日占领，更是雪上加霜，地方饥馑严重，饿殍遍野。

items.en: out of step with the times, ill-timed

ex.h: 那個州的立法單位把不合時宜的法律廢止了。
ex.py: Nà ge zhōu de lì fǎ dān wèi bǎ bù hé shí yí de fǎ lǜ fèi zhǐ le.
ex.en: The state legislature repealed the outdated law.
ex.h_t: 那個州的立法單位把不合時宜的法律廢止了。
ex.h_s: 那个州的立法单位把不合时宜的法律废止了。

origin.text: 秦漢以來之所絕無而僅有
origin.text_s: 秦汉以来之所绝无而仅有

ex.h: 如羅力威這類名符其實的原創作歌手，在香港可說是絕無僅有。
ex.py: Rú Luó Lìwēi zhè lèi míng fú qí shí de yuán chuàng zuò gē shǒu, zài Xiānggǎng kě shuō shì jué wú jǐn yǒu.
ex.en: A true singer-songwriter like Law Lik-wai is almost unheard of in Hong Kong.
ex.h_t: 如羅力威這類名符其實的原創作歌手，在香港可說是絕無僅有。
ex.h_s: 如罗力威这类名符其实的原创作歌手，在香港可说是绝无仅有。

items.note: Wang Chen's praise of wine. "Wine leads one into marvellous places." Now said of books and films.

ex.h: 它產生出大量引人入勝的文學作品，有的存留至今。
ex.py: Tā chǎn shēng chū dà liàng yǐn rén rù shèng de wén xué zuò pǐn, yǒu de cún liú zhì jīn.
ex.en: It produced a great deal of fascinating literature, some of which survives today.
ex.h_t: 它產生出大量引人入勝的文學作品，有的存留至今。
ex.h_s: 它产生出大量引人入胜的文学作品，有的存留至今。

items.en: to add fuel to the fire, to fan

ex.h: 融资买股一定程度上对橡胶的股价起到推波助澜的作用。
ex.py: Róng zī mǎi gǔ yī dìng chéng dù shàng duì xiàng jiāo de gǔ jià qǐ dào tuī bō zhù lán de zuò yòng.
ex.en: Buying shares on borrowed money helped push rubber share prices higher still.
ex.h_t: 融資買股一定程度上對橡膠的股價起到推波助瀾的作用。
ex.h_s: 融资买股一定程度上对橡胶的股价起到推波助澜的作用。

items.note: From a Yuan play. A wife, exiled in the rain, has nowhere to go.

ex.h: 我们被逼得走投无路了。
ex.py: Wǒ men bèi bī de zǒu tóu wú lù le.
ex.en: We've been driven into a corner.
ex.h_t: 我們被逼得走投無路了。
ex.h_s: 我们被逼得走投无路了。

lessons.title: 描寫
lessons.intro: 成語 for describing: where something comes from (來龍去脈), how it is told (輕描淡寫, 淋漓盡致, 直截了當), what is there (應有盡有, 貨真價實), how stable it is (搖搖欲墜, 不堪一擊), how far apart two things are (大相徑庭). Several started in a specialised field: geomancy (來龍去脈), painting and drama (輕描淡寫), Zen (裝模作樣), and a novel (百花齊放, from 鏡花緣).

frames.en: 'coming and going': the whole course of something
two short clauses that mirror each other
欲 'about to': 搖搖欲墜 'swaying, about to fall'
'cannot bear' / 'not enough to'

items.en: the whole story, cause and effect

origin.text: 此間前岡有塊好地，來龍去脈，靠嶺朝山
origin.text_s: 此间前冈有块好地，来龙去脉，靠岭朝山

items.note: A geomancer's term. The "dragon" and "veins" are the lines of hills and rivers that make a site lucky.

ex.h: 我想知道他的计划的来龙去脉。
ex.py: Wǒ xiǎng zhī dào tā de jì huà de lái lóng qù mài.
ex.en: I want to know the ins and outs of his plan.
ex.h_t: 我想知道他的計劃的來龍去脈。
ex.h_s: 我想知道他的计划的来龙去脉。

items.en: to play down, to mention in passing

ex.h: 黃家後裔因有利害衝突，只能對黃南球食言之事輕描淡寫。
ex.py: Huáng jiā hòu yì yīn yǒu lì hài chōng tū, zhǐ néng duì Huáng Nánqiú shí yán zhī shì qīng miáo dàn xiě.
